title: Jarring Malty Syrian Lamb Tagine
description: A hearty and flavorful Syrian dish featuring lamb, pickle, and low-glycemic-friendly ingredients, perfect for a hangover cure.
instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Brown the lamb shoulder pieces on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Remove the lamb from the pot and set aside.
Add more oil if necessary, then sauté the chopped onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper (if using), salt, and black pepper.
Return the lamb to the pot, add the malted barley, pickle juice, and enough water to cover the ingredients.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, for 2 hours.
Uncover and continue to cook for another 30 minutes, or until the sauce has thickened and the lamb is tender.
Taste and adjust the seasoning as needed.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh herbs if desired.
Note: this recipe is for refrigerator pickling/preserving only — store in the refrigerator and consume within 1 week. Do not water-bath can without an acid (vinegar or lemon juice).
